stories.headline: Canada proposes closer European Union ties to protect trade and sovereignty
stories.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg. He called for closer cooperation on defence and energy between Canada and the European Union.

Carney told European lawmakers that closer ties would protect Canada. He said deeper cooperation would stop any external power from controlling Canadian markets. He added that it would prevent outside powers from undermining Canadian sovereignty. Earlier in 2026, Carney spoke at the World Economic Forum. He urged middle powers to act together. He said smaller nations must limit coercive actions by more powerful nations.

Carney proposed new ways to connect citizens across the Atlantic Ocean. He suggested deepening people-to-people ties with the European Union. This proposal would allow young people to live, work, and study on either side of the Atlantic.

Many Canadians share historical links with Europe. According to Canada's 2021 census, over half of the Canadian population reported having European origins. Public opinion also shows support for closer cooperation. An Abacus Data survey conducted before the speech measured public views. It found that 80 percent of Canadians support deepening strategic cooperation with the European Union.

Economic experts view the proposed relationship positively. Fabian Zuleeg, Chief Economist at the European Policy Center, spoke about the economic relationship. Zuleeg said the partnership between Canada and the European Union is a classic win-win situation.

Trade with the United States remains central to the Canadian economy. Up to 72 percent of Canadian exports are destined for the United States.

The proposal faces legal hurdles in Europe. The European Union currently does not have an associate member status. Creating such a status would require approval from all 27 member states.

Political opponents in Canada raised doubts about the initiative. Conservative Member of Parliament Adam Chambers questioned the prime minister's speech. Chambers asked whether Carney's proposal was a concrete plan or just words and vibes.

claims.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney delivered a speech to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, calling for closer bilateral cooperation on defence and energy.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told the European Parliament that closer ties with the EU would prevent any external power from controlling Canada's markets or undermining its sovereignty.
At the World Economic Forum earlier in 2026, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged middle powers to act together to limit coercive actions by more powerful nations.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney proposed deepening people-to-people ties with the EU to allow youth to live, work, and study on either side of the Atlantic.
According to Canada's 2021 census, over half of the Canadian population reported having European origins.
An Abacus Data survey conducted prior to Mark Carney's speech found that 80 percent of Canadians support deepening strategic cooperation with the EU.
Fabian Zuleeg, Chief Economist at the European Policy Center, stated that the partnership between Canada and the European Union is a "classic win-win situation."
Up to 72 percent of Canadian exports are destined for the United States.
The European Union currently does not have an "associate member" status, and establishing one would require approval from all 27 member states.
Conservative Member of Parliament Adam Chambers questioned whether Prime Minister Carney's EU proposal was a concrete plan or "just words and vibes."

vocab.meaning: the authority of a state to govern itself
using force or threats to compel action

stories.headline: UN experts report reasonable grounds US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
stories.body:
United Nations experts reported reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in military strikes in Iran. Two strikes on February 28 killed at least 177 civilians.

Local authorities said a Tomahawk missile hit a primary school in Minab. The strike killed at least 156 people, including 120 children. Iranian state media reported that 168 people died in the school strike. UN investigators concluded the school was the intended target rather than collateral damage. The Pentagon completed an internal investigation into the bombing following reports that targeting data was outdated.

In Lamerd, local officials said missile strikes dispersing tungsten pellets over a sports complex killed at least 21 civilians. US Central Command denied conducting strikes in Lamerd on that date. White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly dismissed the UN report. She said the body had spouted unserious nonsense for decades.

The report also stated Iranian security forces committed crimes against humanity during recent protest crackdowns. Iranian figures reported 3,038 killed, but UN experts believe the true count is higher. Over 70 people in Iran face imminent risk of execution.

claims.text: UN human rights experts reported reasonable grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in two military strikes in Iran on February 28 that killed at least 177 civilians.
Local authorities reported that a Tomahawk missile strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in Minab killed at least 156 people, including 120 children.
Iranian state media reported that 168 people, mostly children, were killed in the February 28 missile strike on the school in Minab.
The UN fact-finding mission concluded that the Minab primary school was the intended point of impact rather than collateral damage from a strike on a nearby IRGC complex.
The Pentagon completed an internal investigation into the Minab school bombing amid reports that US commanders were warned targeting data was outdated.
Local authorities in Lamerd reported that Precision Strike Missiles dispersing tungsten pellets over a sports complex killed at least 21 civilians, including seven children.
US Central Command denied conducting any military strikes in Lamerd on February 28.
White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly dismissed the UN Human Rights Council report, saying the body had spouted "unserious nonsense for decades."
The UN report concluded that Iranian security forces committed crimes against humanity across all 31 provinces during crackdowns on protests in December 2025 and January 2026.
Official Iranian government figures reported that 3,038 people were killed and 25,000 injured during recent protest crackdowns, though UN investigators believe the true count is significantly higher.
UN experts reported that more than 70 people in Iran, including five women and three boys, face imminent risk of execution.

vocab.meaning: unintended damage accompanying a primary objective

stories.headline: Russia begins parliamentary elections during ongoing war in Ukraine
stories.body:
Russian citizens began voting in parliamentary elections for all 450 seats in the State Duma. Voting opened in the Far East regions of Kamchatka and Chukotka. President Vladimir Putin delivered a televised address calling on citizens to demonstrate national unity. He urged voters to show support for Russian troops.

Russia's Supreme Court removed the anti-war Yabloko party from the national ballot. Polling by independent firm ExtremeScan showed 18 percent of Russians would have voted for Yabloko. ExtremeScan also found 60 percent of Russians believe the war in Ukraine negatively affects daily life. According to the Levada Center, six in ten Russians favor peace negotiations with Ukraine.

Exiled opposition leaders Yulia Navalnaya and Maxim Katz asked citizens to vote against United Russia. Opposition politician Ilya Yashin urged anti-war voters to gather at polling stations at noon on September 20. Nearly 200 veterans of the war in Ukraine are running as candidates. Meanwhile, election monitor Grigory Melkonyants was sentenced to five years in prison in 2025.

claims.text: Russians began voting in parliamentary elections, marking the first national parliamentary vote since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
Voting opened in Russia's Far East regions of Kamchatka and Chukotka for all 450 seats in the State Duma.
President Vladimir Putin delivered a televised address calling on citizens to vote to demonstrate national unity and support for Russian troops.
Russia's Supreme Court removed the anti-war Yabloko party from the national election ballot after it had previously been cleared to contest.
A poll by independent research firm ExtremeScan found that 60 percent of Russians believe the war against Ukraine has had negative impacts on their daily lives.
ExtremeScan polling indicated that 18 percent of Russians would have voted for the Yabloko party before it was barred from the ballot.
According to the Levada Center, six in ten Russians favor peace negotiations with Ukraine.
Exiled Russian opposition leaders Yulia Navalnaya and Maxim Katz called on citizens to vote for any party other than United Russia.
Opposition politician Ilya Yashin called on anti-war voters to gather at polling stations at noon on September 20 to demonstrate public opposition.
Russian officials reported that nearly 200 veterans of the war in Ukraine are running as candidates in the parliamentary election.
Grigory Melkonyants, a leader of the independent election monitoring group Golos, was sentenced to five years in prison in 2025 for working with an "undesirable organisation."

vocab.meaning: relating to an elected legislature or parliament

stories.headline: US grants entry visas for Iranian president to attend UN meeting
stories.body:
The United States State Department announced that Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will receive an entry visa. Pezeshkian and a core delegation will attend the UN General Assembly in New York. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Iranian delegation will face travel restrictions. The US also banned the delegation from purchasing luxury goods.

The US government barred Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas from receiving an entry visa for the second straight year. US President Donald Trump said he is approaching a big decision on the next phase of the Iran war. Trump is scheduled to meet leaders from six Gulf nations at the UN headquarters.

Tensions in the region remain high. Iran's Revolutionary Guard struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. The strait handles 20 percent of global seaborne energy transit. Drone attacks on pumping stations temporarily shut down Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. Fighting in Yemen has displaced over 100,000 people inside the country.

claims.text: The US State Department announced that a core Iranian delegation including President Masoud Pezeshkian will be permitted to attend the UN General Assembly High Level Week in New York.
US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott confirmed that the visiting Iranian delegation will face travel restrictions and a ban on purchasing luxury goods.
The US government barred Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas from receiving an entry visa for the UN General Assembly for the second consecutive year.
US President Donald Trump stated in an interview with Axios that he is approaching a "big decision" regarding the next phase of the Iran war.
US President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet leaders from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman at UN headquarters in Manhattan.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that it struck a Togo-flagged oil tanker for making an illegal passage in the Strait of Hormuz.
The Strait of Hormuz handles approximately 20 percent of global seaborne energy transit.
Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, which normally transports 4 million to 5 million barrels of crude oil per day, was temporarily shut down following drone attacks on three pumping stations.
According to the UN refugee agency, recent escalation in Yemen has displaced more than 100,000 people inside the country.

stories.headline: US State Department approves $24 billion F-35 fighter jet deal for Saudi Arabia
stories.body:
The United States State Department notified Congress of a proposed $24.3 billion military sale to Saudi Arabia. The package includes 48 F-35 fighter jets and 49 engines made by Pratt & Whitney.

US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi opposed the deal due to intelligence warnings. He warned that China could gain access to sensitive technology. A US Justice Department case previously involved a Chinese national stealing sensitive military documents from United Technologies.

In July 2026, the US approved a $1.96 billion deal for precision rocket guidance equipment to Saudi Arabia. The US State Department approved another $5 billion sale of over 10,000 bombs in September 2026. Saudi Arabia also signed a mutual defence agreement called the Mecca Agreement with Pakistan and Turkiye.

Conflict along Saudi borders continues. Houthi forces in Yemen claimed they shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet. In Taif province, debris from an intercepted Houthi drone killed one person and injured two others.

claims.text: The US State Department formally notified Congress of a proposed $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.
The $24.3 billion proposed Saudi defence package includes 48 F-35 aircraft and 49 engines manufactured by Pratt & Whitney.
US Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi voiced opposition to the Saudi F-35 deal due to intelligence warnings regarding potential Chinese access to the technology.

A US Justice Department case previously recorded a Chinese national pleading guilty to stealing sensitive military documents from United Technologies and transferring them to benefit China's defence industry.
In July 2026, the US approved a $1.96 billion deal to sell precision rocket guidance equipment to Saudi Arabia.
In September 2026, the US State Department approved a separate $5 billion sale of more than 10,000 bombs to Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defence agreement called the Mecca Agreement with Pakistan and Turkiye.
Houthi forces in Yemen released video footage claiming they shot down a Saudi Arabian F-15 fighter jet over Marib using a locally made surface-to-air missile.
Saudi Arabia reported that debris from an intercepted Houthi drone killed one person and injured two others in Taif province.

vocab.meaning: secret information gathered about an enemy or foreign nation

stories.headline: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson resigns after election defeat
stories.body:
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson submitted his resignation after left-leaning opposition parties won a parliamentary majority. Preliminary counts showed the left-leaning opposition bloc secured 176 seats in the 349-seat Riksdag. The opposition won by a margin of 50,359 votes over the ruling Tidö coalition.

Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson invited three other parties to start initial coalition talks. She reached out to the Left, Centre, and Green parties. Left Party leader Nooshi Dadgostar stated voters gave a clear mandate for change.

The right-wing bloc led by Kristersson secured 173 seats. The far-right Sweden Democrats lost votes in a general election for the first time. The party dropped from second-biggest to third-biggest.

The Speaker of the Riksdag will consult party leaders before nominating a candidate for prime minister. Forming a government took 37 days after the 2022 election and 134 days after the 2018 election.

claims.text: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson announced his resignation after preliminary election counts showed left-leaning opposition parties secured 176 seats in parliament.
Conservative Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson formally submitted his resignation request via a post on social platform X.
Data from the Swedish Election Authority showed the right-wing bloc led by Kristersson secured 173 seats in the 349-seat Riksdag.
The left-leaning opposition bloc secured a narrow three-seat majority over the Tidö coalition, winning by a margin of 50,359 votes.
Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson invited the Left, Centre, and Green parties to begin initial coalition talks.
Left Party leader Nooshi Dadgostar stated that the Swedish electorate "voted away Tidö and given us a clear mandate for change."
The far-right Sweden Democrats suffered a vote loss for the first time in a general election since their founding, dropping from Sweden's second-biggest party to third.
The Speaker of the Riksdag will hold consultations with all party leaders before nominating a candidate for prime minister to be voted on by MPs.
Following the 2022 Swedish election, it required 37 days to form a government, whereas government formation took 134 days after the 2018 election.

vocab.meaning: a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government

stories.headline: US Federal Reserve raises benchmark interest rates for first time since 2023
stories.body:
The United States Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 0.25 percentage points on September 16, 2026. The decision marks the Fed's first interest rate increase in three years. The unanimous vote set the benchmark federal funds rate between 3.75% and 4%. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is too high and has been for too long.

Projections showed 16 out of 18 policymakers expect rates to end 2026 above current levels. President Donald Trump criticized the central bank board. Trump called the board hostile and political for raising rates. Major US banks JPMorgan Chase, KeyCorp, and BNY raised prime lending rates to 7%.

In Singapore, banks increased fixed home loan rates ahead of the Fed decision. Floating-rate loans in Singapore use the Singapore Overnight Rate Average as a benchmark.

High energy costs are causing economic pressures worldwide. Soaring fuel prices sparked public protests in Syria, the Philippines, and Indonesia. Brent crude oil futures fell to $104.82 per barrel on news of possible Saudi oil shipments. The Bank of England kept its interest rate unchanged.

claims.text: The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 0.25 percentage points on September 16, 2026, marking its first interest rate hike since 2023.
The Federal Reserve unanimously voted to raise the benchmark federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to a range of 3.75% to 4%.
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh explained the rate increase by stating that "inflation is too high and has been for too long."
Projections showed that 16 out of 18 Federal Reserve policymakers expect the benchmark rate to end 2026 above its current level.
President Donald Trump publicly criticized the Federal Reserve board, describing it as "hostile" and "political" for raising interest rates.
Major US banks JPMorgan Chase, KeyCorp, and BNY raised their prime lending rates from 6.75% to 7% immediately after the Fed decision.
Singapore banks increased fixed home loan rates by 0.10 to 0.25 percentage points ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate announcement.
Floating-rate home loans in Singapore are benchmarked against the Singapore Overnight Rate Average (SORA).
Soaring fuel prices stemming from the conflict with Iran triggered public street protests in Syria, the Philippines, and Indonesia.
Brent crude oil futures fell one percent to $104.82 per barrel following reports of potential partial restoration of Saudi oil shipments.
The Bank of England kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged during its latest policy meeting.

vocab.meaning: a standard or reference point used for comparison
fully agreed upon by everyone involved

stories.headline: Biologists identify new wild cat species in cloud forests of Bolivia
stories.body:
Biologists named a new wild cat species discovered in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest. The cat is formally named Leopardus tilcayo and locally called tilcayo. The tilcayo measures about 18 inches in length and weighs about 3 pounds.

DNA analysis of 38 specimens showed South American tiger cats consist of five distinct species. Genetic evidence indicates the tilcayo lineage separated from other tiger cats 1.4 million years ago. Biologists also identified a distinct tiger cat subspecies in Peru's Yungas region. The tilcayo is the first newly described living cat species identified since 1923.

Bolivian biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz examined a wild kitten brought to a wildlife sanctuary in 2016. A 10-year-old male tilcayo lives at the Senda Verde sanctuary near La Paz. Local camera traps show the cat is active at night. Scat samples revealed the species eats small rodents. The International Union for Conservation of Nature classifies tiger cats as vulnerable.

claims.text: Biologists formally named and described a new wild cat species, Leopardus tilcayo (locally named tilcayo), discovered in Bolivia's Yungas cloud forest.
Leopardus tilcayo measures approximately 18 inches (46 cm) in length and weighs about 3 pounds (1.4 kg).
Comprehensive DNA analysis of 38 specimens revealed that South American tiger cats consist of five distinct species rather than one.
Genetic analysis estimates that the tilcayo lineage separated from other tiger cats approximately 1.4 million years ago.
Researchers described a distinct tiger cat subspecies in Peru's Yungas region, designating it Leopardus tigrinus antisuyo.
Leopardus tilcayo represents the first newly described living felid species formally identified since the pampas cat in 1923.
In 2016, Bolivian biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz examined a wild kitten brought to Senda Verde wildlife sanctuary after being rescued from a roadside.
A 10-year-old male Leopardus tilcayo currently lives at the Senda Verde Wildlife Sanctuary near La Paz after being surrendered by a local family.
Camera-trap footage indicates that Leopardus tilcayo exhibits nocturnal behavior in the wild.
Scat sample analyses revealed that small rodents constitute part of the diet of Leopardus tilcayo.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature currently classifies tiger cats as two vulnerable species with declining wild populations.

vocab.meaning: direct descent from an ancestor or earlier form

stories.headline: US House approves bill allowing up to 100% tariffs on Indian and Chinese energy imports from Russia
stories.body:
The United States House of Representatives passed legislation granting US President Donald Trump authority to impose high tariffs. The bill allows tariffs of up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil and gas, including India and China. The bill is titled the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026. The House approved the measure by a vote of 262 to 159 after it cleared the Senate.

Under the draft law, 100% tariffs could apply to the five largest importers of Russian oil or gas. The duties would target countries that knowingly continue purchases 30 days after the bill becomes law.

Indian officials defended their energy purchases. India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra said energy is a vital strategic necessity for 1.4 billion Indians. Kwatra called energy the foundation of India's development. India imports over 85% of its crude oil and about half of its natural gas.

Trade relations between the US and India have faced past friction. In April 2025, the US announced a 26% tariff on several Indian imports. The US paused that rate for 90 days before setting a temporary 10% duty.

China also criticized the US legislation. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said China opposes unilateral sanctions that lack a UN Security Council mandate. Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington on September 24-25 for a summit with Trump. US and Chinese officials are consulting on a tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion in products from each side.

claims.text: The US House of Representatives passed legislation granting US President Donald Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries continuing to buy Russian oil and gas, including India and China.
The legislation passed by the US House of Representatives is titled the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act 2026.
The US House of Representatives approved the sanctions bill by a vote of 262 to 159 after it cleared the Senate.
The US draft law states that 100% tariffs could apply to the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or natural gas if they knowingly continue purchases 30 days after enactment.
India's Ambassador to the US Vinay Mohan Kwatra stated that energy is a vital strategic necessity for 1.4 billion Indians and the foundation of India's development.
India imports over 85% of its crude oil and around half of its natural gas.
In April 2025, the US announced a 26% tariff on several Indian imports before pausing it for 90 days and imposing a temporary 10% duty.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun stated that China opposes long-arm jurisdiction and unilateral sanctions that lack a UN Security Council mandate.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to visit Washington on September 24-25 for a summit with US President Donald Trump.
China and the US are consulting on a reciprocal tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products from each side.

vocab.meaning: taxes imposed by a government on imported goods
penalties applied against a nation to force compliance with laws
action taken by one nation without agreement from others

stories.headline: Election Commission freezes Trinamool Congress name and symbol following party split
stories.body:
The Election Commission of India froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and party symbol. The interim order came after rival party factions split. The order prevents both groups from using the flowers and grass symbol. The Election Commission issued the decision under Paragraph 15 of the 1968 Election Symbols Order.

The freezing order applies to upcoming elections. The commission barred both factions from using the party name and symbol for the October 6 parliamentary by-election in Assam's Nagaon seat. West Bengal will also hold assembly by-elections in Rejinagar and Nandigram on October 6. The Election Commission instructed both factions to submit three new group names and symbol choices from the free symbols list.

Party leaders reacted strongly to the decision. Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee accused Ritabrata Banerjee of triggering the dispute because he was not named opposition leader. Congress General Secretary K.C. Venugopal criticized the order. Venugopal called the decision a bullet through the heart of Indian democracy.

claims.text: The Election Commission of India froze the All India Trinamool Congress's reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol and party name in an interim order following a split between rival factions.
The Election Commission of India issued its interim order under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation & Allotment) Order, 1968.
The Election Commission barred both Trinamool Congress factions from using the party name and symbol for the October 6 parliamentary by-election in Assam's Nagaon seat.
Assembly by-elections in West Bengal's Rejinagar and Nandigram seats are scheduled for October 6.
The Election Commission directed both factions to submit three preferred temporary group names and three symbol choices from the free symbols list by 11 a.m. on Friday.
Trinamool Congress MP Kalyan Banerjee alleged that Ritabrata Banerjee orchestrated the internal dispute because he was not selected as the opposition leader.
Congress General Secretary K.C. Venugopal described the freezing of the All India Trinamool Congress symbol as a 'bullet through the heart of Indian democracy'.

vocab.meaning: temporary or serving in the time between two events
small dissenting groups within a larger political party

stories.headline: Indian government establishes fee rules for digital UPI transactions above Rs 2,000
stories.body:
The Indian government announced that a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 starting October 15. Small merchants earning up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes will be exempt. Finance Ministry sources estimate that transactions above Rs 2,000 make up about 4% of total UPI transaction volume.

The National Payments Corporation of India set a flat Rs 5 rate per transaction above Rs 2,000 for specific sectors. These sectors include railways, telecom, insurance, and fuel. The Payments Council of India confirmed the flat Rs 5 fee applies to fuel purchases. The Department of Financial Services said 5% of fee collections will fund a dedicated fund to promote UPI adoption among small merchants.

Industry figures held differing views on the fee structure. BharatPe CEO Nalin Negi said UPI will remain free for consumers while building a sustainable ecosystem. Former BharatPe CEO Ashneer Grover claimed merchants will pass the cost on to customers. Meanwhile, the Department of Financial Services rejected claims of US influence. Official rules restrict UPI credit transactions to RuPay cards.

claims.text: The Indian government announced that a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 starting October 15.
Small merchants earning up to Rs 1 lakh per month through UPI QR codes will be exempt from the new Merchant Discount Rate charges.
Finance Ministry sources estimate that UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 represent approximately 4% of total UPI transaction volume.
The National Payments Corporation of India set a flat Merchant Discount Rate of Rs 5 per transaction above Rs 2,000 for specific categories including railways, telecom, insurance, and fuel.
The Payments Council of India clarified that a flat Rs 5 Merchant Discount Rate applies to UPI fuel transactions above Rs 2,000, disputing claims that a 0.4% rate would apply.
The Department of Financial Services stated that a dedicated fund funded by 5% of Merchant Discount Rate collections will be established to promote UPI adoption among small merchants.
BharatPe CEO Nalin Negi stated that the new Merchant Discount Rate framework proves UPI will remain free for consumers while building a sustainable payments ecosystem.
Former BharatPe CEO Ashneer Grover criticized the UPI merchant fee, claiming that the cost will eventually be passed on to the customer.
The Department of Financial Services rejected claims of US influence, stating that the September 15 NPCI circular restricts UPI credit transactions exclusively to RuPay credit cards.

vocab.meaning: free from an obligation or requirement that applies to others
